question: Will AfD win the most seats in the 2026 Berlin state elections?
resolution_criteria:
Parliamentary elections to elect the Abgeordnetehaus of Berlin are scheduled to take place in Berlin on September 20, 2026.

This market will resolve to the political party that wins the greatest number of seats in the formal deliberative assembly of Berlin (Abgeordnetenhaus) as a result of this election.

If voting in the Berlin election for the Abgeordnetenhaus does not occur by December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the case of a tie between this party or coalition and any other for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose listed abbreviation comes first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Election Office of Berlin (Landeswahlleiter Berlin https://www.berlin.de/wahlen/)

# Research report 1 of 2

# AfD and the most seats in the 2026 Berlin election: research notes (as of 2026-09-16)

Page fetches kept failing (the proxy refused the connection), so most facts below come from search-result summaries of the cited pages. They have not been checked directly. Some results also contained material dated after 2026-09-16. I left all of it out.

## 1. Resolution source
- The 2023 repeat election is the most recent official baseline. CDU came first with about 28.2% and won the most seats. AfD got about 9.1% and 17 seats. [statista](https://de.statista.com/statistik/daten/studie/3114/umfrage/endergebnis-der-wahl-zum-abgeordnetenhaus-in-berlin)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Voting is still four days away. AfD has never been the largest party in the Abgeordnetenhaus. In none of the September polls I found was AfD in first place.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-13: Prediction Hunt ran an article saying "Linke leads Berlin polls but internal paper…". I could only see the headline. [predictionhunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/linke-leads-berlin-polls-but-internal-paper-sep-13-2026)
- 2026-09-11: Forschungsgruppe Wahlen for ZDF (Politbarometer Extra): Linke 23, CDU 21, AfD 17, Grüne 16, SPD 10. ZDF called it a two-way race between Linke and CDU. The fieldwork came after the Saxony-Anhalt election. [ZDF](https://www.zdfheute.de/politik/deutschland/berlin-wahl-abgeordnetenhaus-politbarometer-extra-100.html)
- About 2026-09-10: Infratest dimap for ARD: Linke 21, CDU 20, AfD 18, Grüne 16, SPD 12, BSW 4. Infratest described it as neck and neck. [Infratest dimap](https://www.infratest-dimap.de/umfragen-analysen/bundeslaender/berlin/laendertrend/2026/september-ii/)
- 2026-09-07: After the AfD landslide in Saxony-Anhalt (it narrowly missed an absolute majority), its market odds of winning Berlin reportedly doubled from about 8% to 18%. Polls still had AfD third or fourth in Berlin. [predictionhunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/afd-berlin-win-odds-double-to-18-after-saxony-sep-07-2026)
- 2026-09-04: INSA for BILD: CDU 20, Linke 19, AfD 18, Grüne 15, SPD 15, BSW 3. AfD was up 1 point from 14 August. [DAWUM](https://dawum.de/Berlin/INSA/2026-09-04/)
- Undated, around early September: one INSA poll had AfD in second place for the first time, behind CDU. [Berliner Kurier](https://www.berliner-kurier.de/article/berlin-wahl-steht-bevor-afd-ist-laut-umfrage-jetzt-die-zweitstaerkste-kraft-10021047)
- 2026-08-27 to 08-31: Infratest dimap for RBB: CDU 21, Linke 19, AfD third (number not given in the summary). [dawum Infratest](https://dawum.de/Berlin/Infratest_dimap/)
- 2026-08-04 to 08-18: Forsa: Linke 22, CDU 18, AfD 18, Grüne 16, SPD 12. [t-online](https://www.t-online.de/nachrichten/deutschland/innenpolitik/id_101374354/berlin-wahl-2026-wahlumfragen-zeichnen-knappes-rennen-ums-abgeordnetenhaus.html)
- About 2026-07-21: INSA had AfD first at 19, with CDU and Linke both at 18. This is the only poll I found with AfD in the lead. [infranken](https://www.infranken.de/deutschland/insa-umfrage-afd-in-berlin-auf-platz-eins-art-6382690,PRINT), [politpro](https://politpro.eu/en/berlin/opinion-polls/insa-2026-07-21/state-election)

## 4. Base rates
- Berlin elections before 2026 (2016, 2021, 2023): AfD's best result was about 14% in 2016. It has never come first.
- In 2026 polling, AfD has mostly sat at 16-19%, usually third, 1-6 points behind the leader. Only one poll (INSA, July) had it first. In the September polls I found, AfD trailed the leader by 2-6 points.
- In the 2026 cycle, the gap between the top three parties has been within the typical error of a state poll (about ±3 points). Berlin polls have historically missed by 2-4 points for individual parties.
- The seat count tracks vote share closely: seats are allocated proportionally with a 5% threshold, and overhang seats are compensated. So whichever party has the most votes should also have the most seats.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-05-18: Polymarket (via Orrery) had CDU at 34%, Grüne 28%, Linke 20%, SPD 6%. [orrery](https://www.orrery.me/markets/will-cdu-win-the-most-seats-in-the-2026-berlin-state-elections)
- 2026-08-21: Linke was at about 39% to win the most seats, with CDU close behind. [predictionhunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/berlin-election-polls-linke-odds-39-aug-21-2026)
- 2026-09-07: AfD was at about 18%. [predictionhunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/afd-berlin-win-odds-double-to-18-after-saxony-sep-07-2026)
- About 2026-09-11: Linke was at about 58%, then about 68-69% on Kalshi and Polymarket after the mid-September polls. AfD was reported at roughly 16-18%. These come from a secondary aggregator. [predictionhunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/linke-hits-58-in-berlin-election-market-sep-11-2026)
- I also saw an undated quote of 11¢ for AfD's most-seats contract, which may be stale. [simplefunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/berlin-state-election-winner-afd-polymarket-0x8aaaca6ea5)
- I could not find any Manifold market or independent expert seat model.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More polls may appear before the vote, possibly from INSA, Forsa, Civey or YouGov. German pollsters usually stop publishing in the last days before an election.
- Factors that could still move things: late shifts after the Saxony-Anhalt result, turnout, and BSW or FDP falling under or getting over the 5% threshold, which changes how seats are split.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

The AfD is clearly in third place in every poll found up to 2026-09-14. It sits at 17-18%, about 2-4 points behind both Die Linke and the CDU, and nothing has happened yet that settles the question.

## 1. Resolution source
- The Abgeordnetenhaus has at least 130 seats, filled by proportional representation. Overhang and balancing seats are possible. In polling-based seat models, the party with the most list votes generally gets the most seats.

## 2. Current status
- In every poll I found from late August to 2026-09-14, the AfD is third.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-14: INSA poll for BILD: CDU 20%, Linke 20%, AfD 18%, Greens 16%, SPD 12%. [dawum](https://dawum.de/Berlin/INSA/2026-09-14/)
- 2026-09-10: Infratest dimap BerlinTREND for ARD (fieldwork 7-9 Sept): Linke 21%, CDU 20%, AfD 18%, Greens 16%, SPD 12%. Only 9% of voters are satisfied with AfD lead candidate Kristin Brinker, and about two-thirds cannot rate her. [infratest dimap](https://www.infratest-dimap.de/umfragen-analysen/bundeslaender/berlin/laendertrend/2026/september-ii/), [dawum](https://dawum.de/Berlin/Infratest_dimap/2026-09-10/)
- 2026-09-04: INSA: CDU 20%, Linke 19%, AfD 18%, Greens 15%, SPD 15%. [dawum](https://dawum.de/Berlin/INSA/2026-09-04/)
- 2026-08-22: Forsa: Linke 22%, AfD 18%, CDU 18%, Greens 16%, SPD 12%, BSW 4%, FDP 3%. This is the AfD's best relative position: tied for second, 4 points behind first. [dawum](https://dawum.de/Berlin/Forsa/2026-08-22/), [t-online](https://www.t-online.de/nachrichten/deutschland/innenpolitik/id_101399250/neue-umfrage-berlin-wahl-2026-linke-legen-zu-afd-und-cdu-gleichauf.html)
- August 2026: In a Civey direct-election question, Brinker came second with 15%, behind CDU candidate Stefan Evers at 20%. This comes from a search snippet that I could not open. [zdfheute candidate overview](https://www.zdfheute.de/politik/deutschland/berlin-wahl-2026-spitzenkandidaten-cdu-spd-gruene-linke-afd-100.html)
- Media are framing the race as a CDU vs Linke contest for first place, and say three-party coalitions are needed. [t-online](https://www.t-online.de/nachrichten/deutschland/innenpolitik/id_101374354/wahlumfrage-zur-berlin-wahl-2026-eine-partei-setzt-sich-im-rennen-ab.html)

## 4. Base rates
- The AfD has never finished first in a Berlin state election. It got 9.1% in the 2023 repeat election, 8.0% in 2021 and 14.2% in 2016 (these figures are from my background knowledge). In 2023 the CDU won with about 28%. Polls now show the AfD roughly doubling its 2023 share, but still behind.
- In German state elections, the final-week polling leader usually wins. A party that is third and 2-4 points behind rarely ends up first. The usual polling error per party in German state elections is about 1-3 points. Berlin has a fragmented five-party field where the top three are within about 2-4 points, so upsets are plausible in general. For the AfD to finish first, though, it would need to beat both the CDU and Die Linke at once.
- The AfD has finished first in eastern state elections before, for example Thuringia in 2024, but Berlin's electorate is far less favourable to it, especially in the western boroughs.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket "Will AfD win the most seats in the 2026 Berlin state elections?" was at about 11 cents (11%) around 2026-04-21/22, according to a SimpleFunctions mirror. I could not fetch the page to check a later price. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/berlin-state-election-winner-afd-polymarket-0x8aaaca6ea5)
- Polymarket mirror snapshots from 2026-05-18 (Orrery) show CDU about 34%, Greens about 28%, Linke about 20%, SPD about 6%. I found no AfD figure for that date. [CDU](https://www.orrery.me/markets/will-cdu-win-the-most-seats-in-the-2026-berlin-state-elections), [Linke](https://www.orrery.me/markets/will-linke-win-the-most-seats-in-the-2026-berlin-state-elections)
- I could not find any September 2026 market prices, or any Kalshi or Manifold markets.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The last polls of the final week may come out around 2026-09-17/18. ZDF Politbarometer and Forsa are typical, but I have not confirmed specific releases.
- The tie-break favours the earliest abbreviation alphabetically, and "AfD" would come first. That only matters if the AfD exactly ties for the most seats.

- INSA in July 2026 had AfD first at 19.
  - The Saxony-Anhalt landslide (around 2026-09-06) gave AfD momentum, and markets doubled its odds to about 18% on 2026-09-07.
  - AfD has sometimes slightly outperformed its polls.
- **For No:**
  - Forsa on 2026-08-22: Linke 22, AfD 18.
  - Infratest dimap on 2026-09-10: Linke 21, CDU 20, AfD 18.
  - Forschungsgruppe Wahlen (ZDF) on 2026-09-11: Linke 23, CDU 21, AfD 17.
  - AfD's lead candidate, Brinker, has weak ratings: 9% satisfaction.
  - Media frame the race as Linke versus CDU.
  - Markets moved to about 68% for Linke by mid-September.

**(e) Scenarios:**
- **No:** Linke consolidates the left vote and wins about 22%, CDU gets about 21%, and AfD lands around 17-18%, a clear third.
- **Yes:** A late swing after Saxony-Anhalt and differential turnout push AfD to about 21%, while the vote splits evenly between CDU and Linke at about 20% each. AfD edges out both by a few tenths.

**(f) From base rate to final probability:** AfD needs roughly a 2-5 point relative swing against both leaders at once. This is plausible within typical polling error, but the outcomes for the two leaders are correlated and AfD has to beat the better of them, which lowers its chances. Market prices were around 16-18% on 2026-09-07 to 09-11, likely somewhat inflated by enthusiasm after Saxony-Anhalt. The latest polls show no AfD surge. I move up slightly from the 8% base for the tight race and the INSA closeness, and stay below the market.

Probability: 11%

- AfD is third in every poll from late August to 2026-09-14.
  - Forschungsgruppe Wahlen (2026-09-11) had AfD 6 points behind Linke.
  - Infratest (2026-09-10) had it 3 points behind.
  - Lead candidate Brinker is weak: only 9% are satisfied with her and two-thirds cannot rate her.
  - Berlin's western boroughs are hostile to AfD.
  - The media frame the race as Linke vs CDU, so tactical voting is likely to consolidate behind those two.

**(e) Scenarios**
- No: Linke consolidates the left vote and finishes around 22%, CDU around 21%, and AfD around 17-18%. This matches the polls and the historical pattern of AfD meeting or slightly missing its Berlin polls.
- Yes: Momentum from Saxony-Anhalt plus a shy-voter polling error pushes AfD to about 21%. At the same time, the left vote splits between Linke, Greens and SPD, and the CDU sags to about 19-20%. AfD then edges both by a fraction of a point.

**(f) From base rate to final probability**
I start at about 7%. The race is unusually tight, with the top three often within 2-3 points, and the Saxony-Anhalt momentum is a real factor, so I move up to about 9-10%. The market at about 16-18% is a reference point, but I discount it. These markets tend to overprice longshots, and the figures come from a secondary aggregator rather than a verified current price. Fresh polls after Saxony-Anhalt (FGW and Infratest, 2026-09-10/11) still show AfD clearly third, which argues against the market's level. I settle at about 9%.

Probability: 9%

(e) No scenario: Linke consolidates the left vote in the final days and the CDU holds its base. AfD finishes at 17-19% in third, behind two parties at 21-23%.

Yes scenario: polls underestimate AfD by 2-3 points, as happened in some eastern elections. Left-wing votes split between Linke, Greens and SPD, and the CDU falls to about 18%. AfD edges first at around 20%.

(f) Close top-three polling and a possible systematic polling miss favouring AfD lift me slightly above the base rate. The reported market price of about 16-18% also pulls me upward. However, that figure comes from a secondary aggregator, was partly measured right after the Saxony-Anhalt news, and is not supported by later polls. So I don't fully defer to it. I end up near 9%.

Probability: 9%
